symptom: A GitHub contents write inserted literal backslash-n text rather than line breaks in a new TypeScript helper. Two already-triggered research-governance jobs on unchanged code reported TS1128 at line 257 with process exit 1; checkout/post-job cleanup completed and no runner/platform fault was evidenced. The source was read back and corrected in a materially changed commit before any third identical attempt.
lesson: A string used to construct source content can contain escaped newline characters rather than actual line breaks. Multiple workflows triggered by adjacent commits may repeat the same unchanged parse failure; a new main SHA or extra workflow does not change that root cause.
guardrail: Before writing generated source through the GitHub contents API, inspect the exact inserted lines or parse a local equivalent. After a write, fetch the exact branch file and verify real line breaks before relying on CI. Treat repeated TS1128 at the same source line as the same fingerprint; repair the source representation rather than retrying unchanged workflows.
